note: a question a verb invited, about an open case

74.label: A Word in the Right Ear
74.desc: An informer trusts you now, which in this city is rarer than gold. They tell you which tapster to buy, and which to be seen buying. (In Rest on its own it is a lesson: one more Instinct, for good. With your Instinct beside it, it is kept as a trick instead: Informers bring word sooner.)

80.desc: The bands have sworn to one shell now, and the shell has a king: Regina Dyer, the King of Thunes, on a barrel in a cellar under the Warrens. The Vendetta surges every week. Go in Disguise: with the ledger, to break it; with Wit, to parley; with Instinct and Coin, to be tried by its court and stay.

100.label: The Sergeant's Patience
100.desc: The sergeant has seen every examiner burn out the same way. He shows you how he sits down between things: how he lets a case go for the length of a pipe, and comes back to it. (In Rest on its own it is a lesson: one more Wit, for good. With your Wit beside it, it is kept as a trick instead: Spent Health, Wit and Instinct come back in half the time.)

117.label: The Old Examiner's Method
117.desc: Full proof before the Blood Court, and the judge asked who taught you. Nobody did. But in the drawer of your desk is a leaf in the last examiner's hand, and reading it now, you understand it. (In Rest on its own it is a lesson: one more Wit, for good. With your Wit beside it, it is kept as a trick instead: Witnesses keep half again as long before they forget.)

131.label: The Market
131.desc: Stalls, the weigh-house, pawnbrokers and cutpurses. The pillory stands in the square, and your Watch-house at its edge.

155.label: Petition: The Hole
155.desc: A cell under the Watch-house with a table and one candle. Questioning is faster and draws out more Word. Costs 8 Coin.

157.label: Petition: The Rolls
157.desc: The court's old books, shelved and indexed. Unanswered cases can be opened again in Study. Costs 8 Coin.

158.label: Petition: The Thief-takers' Office
158.desc: A room let to men who know every fence in the city. Put a Case in Attend with 2 Coin and they get the goods back for a cut, without a trial. Some of what they bring back is a frame. Costs 6 Coin.

173.label: Letter: Sergeant of the Watch
173.desc: Thirty years with a halberd. Has seen this before. Has seen everything before, and hanged some of it. Costs 5 Coin.

176.label: An Iron Constitution
176.desc: Hunger, fever and the black nights, and you are still at the desk. The Warrens give everything to everyone in the end, and you have found out what they cannot take. (In Rest on its own it is a lesson: one more Health, for good. With your Health beside it, it is kept as a trick instead: The needs come for you less often.)

177.label: Petition: Lantern and Cloak
177.desc: A dark lantern with a shutter, a cloak that is nobody's. Opens the Watch whatever your office, and turns a night in a doorway into names and hours written down. Costs 6 Coin.

178.label: Petition: The Informers' Bench
178.desc: A bench by the back door where the city's whisperers wait. A token that points at a front names it at once; the Coquille shows itself. Costs 6 Coin.

179.label: Petition: The Drill Yard
179.desc: Drilling a watchman costs 1 Coin instead of 2, and at the third drill they learn a new trait. Costs 8 Coin.

187.label: Confessor Kuiper
187.desc: A priest without a parish. Sits. Listens. People tell him things they have never told God. Slot them into a verb to help. Patient: Study and the Watch take a fifth less time.

192.label: Petition: Physician's Case
192.desc: Lancets, a silver needle, dried herbs in paper twists. Needed for blood and poison, sharpens anything of the body, and finds more of it at a scene. Costs 5 Coin.

193.label: Petition: Strongroom
193.desc: Tokens and raw proof keep twice as long behind an iron door. Costs 6 Coin.

213.label: Fire at the Molenaar Warehouse
213.desc: Somebody set fire to the Molenaar Warehouse a day after the refusal. It started with a cobble with a note tied to it. The message came the next morning: the name of a tavern. (The Market)

218.label: The Warrens
218.desc: Tenements stacked against the wall, and cellars under the cellars. Everyone saw nothing, and everyone knows everything.

230.label: Heard on the Round
230.desc: Regina Kuiper heard it at the conduit, about Fire at the Molenaar Warehouse: "They were chewing something. Cloves, I thought."

231.label: The Message
231.desc: the name of a tavern. This was not the first, and it was not meant to be the last.

232.label: A Tavern Token: the washhouse in Weber Row
232.desc: A lead token from the washhouse in Weber Row, the kind they give for a drink owed. Rubbed smooth. A chit in a drawer keeps.

233.label: Hans Seiler
233.desc: Hans Seiler, the building's owner. Has had a key to the house for years. (Accused in: Fire at the Molenaar Warehouse)

245.label: A Chewed Clove
245.desc: A clove, chewed flat and spat behind the stove. Somebody with a bad tooth stood here a while.

249.label: ★ The Death of Endres Ebner
249.desc: Endres Ebner sickened over a month: hair coming out in the comb. Everyone called it a wasting. The coroner's book calls it something else. In the sickroom, a bottle of "tonic". (The Market) The crier has sung it: the whole city is watching.

teammate.label: Beadle Pietersz
teammate.desc: A parish beadle with a staff and a loud voice. Knocks on doors without complaining and whips beggars without being asked. Slot them into a verb to help. Thorough: Finds one more thing at every scene.

255.label: Letter: Apothecary's Boy
255.desc: Talks to jars more than people. Knows the taste of every powder in the shop and which ones he should not have tasted. Costs 3 Coin.

256.label: Deposition: Matthes Mercer
256.desc: "Big boots. Nailed. You could hear them coming on the cobbles." (Wants the reward.)

data.who: a child who could not sleep

257.label: Witness: Ursel Kessler
257.desc: Ursel Kessler, a child who could not sleep. Was at their casement and saw somebody near the Molenaar Warehouse, and is fond of somebody in the case. (Witness in: Fire at the Molenaar Warehouse)

258.label: Hodge de Witt
258.desc: Hodge de Witt, a tenant put out. Drives a dray with a lame grey mule. (Accused in: Fire at the Molenaar Warehouse)

259.label: Witness: Barent Fletcher
259.desc: Barent Fletcher, a man on the bucket-chain. Was at their casement and saw somebody near the Molenaar Warehouse, and has an old grudge in the quarter. (Witness in: Fire at the Molenaar Warehouse)

260.label: Bartel Bakker
260.desc: Bartel Bakker, the night-clerk. Chews cloves against the toothache, constantly. (Accused in: Fire at the Molenaar Warehouse)

272.label: The Council's Letter: Magistrate
272.desc: Muster the Watch and have cases cried (Attend), and a city that expects everything of you. Attend on the Council.

teammate.label: Apothecary's Boy Vos
teammate.desc: Talks to jars more than people. Knows the taste of every powder in the shop and which ones he should not have tasted. Slot them into a verb to help. Sharp: Reads raw proof properly even without the right instrument.

ask.label: A shut door
ask.text: One house will not open to the Watch. It opens to Coin. Shut, it keeps what it knows.

c10.title: Burglary at the Molenaar House

vars.detail: a tradesman's cart that no tradesman came from

suspects.name: Barbel Tucher
suspects.motive: Let go without a letter, and still talking of it in every tavern in the Stews.
suspects.alibi: a bed in the Abbey hospital

suspects.name: Afra Chandler
suspects.motive: The nephew was cut out of the will a week ago, loudly, at table.
suspects.alibi: a game of tables with a sergeant of the Watch

suspects.name: Dorcas Webster
suspects.motive: The porter was turned off last month and never paid his last wages.

items.label: Marks on the Sill
items.text: The print of a hand on the whitewash. Faint, but there.

result.label: The Hand Read
result.text: Under vinegar and the red umbrella the hand comes up whole: a thumb with a scar across it. Good enough for the Court.

items.label: Pipe Ash in the Study
items.text: Nobody in the house smokes.

result.label: The Tobacco Named
result.text: Cheap leaf, sold at two shops in the city. Both keep a slate for regulars.

items.label: A Shell on the Sill
items.text: A cockle-shell, the Compostela kind, on the sill where a hat was set down.

items.label: The Second Key
items.text: The strongbox was opened, not forced. Three people have a key. One of them lent it.

witnesses: the woman at the casement opposite

c27.title: False Coin in Gerber's Tavern

vars.time: on Sunday, when the forges are cold
vars.detail: smoke from a chimney where nobody lives

suspects.name: Sibylla de Groot
suspects.motive: The journeyman has the hands for a die and none of the guild's scruples.

suspects.name: Walburg Bicker
suspects.motive: The soldier learned to cast bullets in Flanders and found a better use for lead.

suspects.name: Gregory Schmidt
suspects.motive: The tavern passes more coin in a night than the Mint in a week, and nobody looks at it by candlelight.

items.label: Smoke After Curfew
items.text: smoke from a chimney where nobody lives. No forge is licensed there.

items.label: A Plaster Mould
items.text: Broken in half in a midden.

result.label: The Mould Read
result.text: Vinegar brings up the hand that pressed the plaster: a thumb, and a missing nail.

items.label: A broken mould
items.text: Thrown away in a hurry.

result.label: The Hand on the Mould
result.text: Vinegar brings up the hand that pressed it: a thumb, and a missing nail.

items.label: A Lombard's Chit
items.text: A chit from across the river for a coat, redeemed and pledged again. Somebody lives from Friday to Friday.

witnesses: a market-woman who was paid in it

c90.title: Hue and Cry: Regina Dyer
c90.scene: a Rented Garret in The Abbey Close

vars.scene: a Rented Garret in The Abbey Close

suspects.name: Regina Dyer
suspects.motive: They know you are coming. They have always known.

items.label: Disturbed Dust
items.text: Something heavy was moved lately. Lately enough to date it.

items.label: The Old Case
items.text: Your notes from the first time round. You were closer than you knew.

items.label: A Curved Scratch
items.text: A fresh curved scratch in the wax of the table, the kind a heavy signet leaves on a clenched fist.

items.label: The Abandoned Garret
items.text: Left in a hurry. A cup on the table.

result.label: The Hand on the Cup
result.text: The same hand as the one in the Rolls from the first case.

c141.title: Burglary at Fletcher's Pawnshop

vars.entry: the stair from the rooms above
vars.item: three silver spoons and a ledger
vars.detail: the candle go on and off again, as if someone knew the house

suspects.name: Cicely Hobson
suspects.motive: The partnership is drowning in debt, and a theft is a loss the guild will forgive.

suspects.name: Hodge Welser
suspects.motive: The nephew was cut out of the will a week ago, loudly, at table.
suspects.alibi: a wedding, and forty guests who remember the dancing

suspects.name: Griet Claesz
suspects.motive: Let go without a letter, and still talking of it in every tavern in the Stews.

items.label: The Key Tally
items.text: Who has keys, and since when. Someone has crossed a name out.

result.label: The Key-holders
result.text: Four keys. Three are accounted for. The fourth was "lost" a month ago by someone who still comes and goes.

items.label: The Carrier's Chit
items.text: A carrier's chit for a place on Friday's wagon to the coast. One way. Someone is planning to leave.

items.label: A Chit from the washhouse in Weber Row
items.text: Folded small, in the wrong pocket. A chit from the washhouse in Weber Row, dated last week. A chit in a drawer keeps.

items.label: A Key, Not a Crow
items.text: the stair from the rooms above: no marks, no damage. Whoever came in was expected, or had a key.

witnesses: the woman at the casement opposite

c212.title: Fire at the Molenaar Warehouse

vars.detail: a cobble with a note tied to it

suspects.name: Bartel Bakker
suspects.motive: The clerk had been skimming from the books, and the books were in the counting-room.

suspects.name: Hans Seiler
suspects.motive: The building was pledged for three times its worth, and the owner was ruined.

suspects.name: Hodge de Witt
suspects.motive: The tenant had been put into the street two days before the fire.

items.label: The Message
items.text: the name of a tavern. This was not the first, and it was not meant to be the last.

items.label: A Tavern Token: the washhouse in Weber Row
items.text: A lead token from the washhouse in Weber Row, the kind they give for a drink owed. Rubbed smooth. A chit in a drawer keeps.

items.label: A cobble with a note tied to it
items.text: What the fire started with. Cheap, and handled.

result.label: The Hand on the Kindling
result.text: A clean thumb on the one part that did not burn.

items.label: A Chewed Clove
items.text: A clove, chewed flat and spat behind the stove. Somebody with a bad tooth stood here a while.

witnesses: a drunk asleep in the doorway opposite

c248.title: The Death of Endres Ebner
c248.scene: a Cell in the Abbey Hospital

vars.scene: a Cell in the Abbey Hospital
vars.detail: hair coming out in the comb

suspects.name: Dorcas Molenaar
suspects.motive: The cook was beaten in this house, and everyone in the kitchen knew it.

suspects.name: Els Sattler
suspects.motive: The heir had been living on expectations, and the expectations had run out.

suspects.name: Barent Holzschuher
suspects.motive: The apothecary sold the powder, and had been paid to forget who bought it.

items.label: The Course of It
items.text: hair coming out in the comb. A sickness that keeps a timetable is not a sickness.

items.label: A Hobnail Scar
items.text: A deep gouge at the foot of the door, the kind a hobnailed boot makes. A big boot, and a kick.

items.label: Disturbed Dust
items.text: Something heavy was moved lately. Lately enough to date it.

items.label: A bottle of "tonic"
items.text: Taken every day, by one person only.

result.label: The Needle Blackens
result.text: Silver into the dregs, out black. A little every day, for a month.

journal.title: The Pawnbroker's Book
journal.text: A pawnbroker keeps a book of everything that came through his door this week, and who brought it. Something from your case is in it. He would part with the page. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Week 16
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 2. The Council's stipend: 3 Coin. A name you let go was heard in the Red Ox this week. There is a purse on your desk. Nobody saw who left it. The ledger: 1 conviction; 2 open; 6 Coin in hand.

journal.title: A Watchman Hurt
journal.text: Apothecary's Boy Vos was set upon outside the Watch-house. They will be in the Abbey hospital for a while.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: The Cough Clears
journal.text: Bitter bark in wine, two days sweating under every blanket you own, and on the third morning the river smells like a river again.

journal.title: Healed
journal.text: The barber-surgeon takes the stitches out. You can take a blow again. Probably.

journal.title: The Council Takes Notice
journal.text: A letter on heavy paper under the city's seal: the Council will see you about the office of Magistrate. Attend on them, in a clean collar.

journal.title: Guilty: Griet Claesz
journal.text: The sworn men are out for the length of a Paternoster. Griet Claesz is convicted of Burglary at Fletcher's Pawnshop, and the sergeants take them down to the Hole to wait for the sentence. The Council's thanks, with a purse attached.

journal.title: The Inquisitor: Griet Claesz
journal.text: The Inquisitor takes Griet Claesz out of the Hole before you can speak. The question is applied whether you would or not, a confession is read out, and the Fire follows by the end of the week. He thanks you for your diligence in finding the heretic. You did not know there was one.

journal.title: Door to Door
journal.text: Around the Molenaar Warehouse people are frightened, and frightened people talk. You come away with: Witness: Ursel Kessler; Hodge de Witt (accused); Witness: Barent Fletcher; Bartel Bakker (accused). One door stayed shut, and the street talked less for it.

journal.title: Interrupted
journal.text: Whatever you were working on is gone before you finish. The city does not wait.

journal.title: A Long Rest
journal.text: A week of nothing. Long walks outside the walls. Small beer and bread. Your hands stop shaking on the fourth day. On the seventh you want to go back to the Watch-house, which is either a good sign or a very bad one.

journal.title: A Deposition
journal.text: Matthes Mercer keeps begging your pardon for wasting your time. They are not wasting it. "Big boots. Nailed. You could hear them coming on the cobbles."

journal.title: Week 15
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 2. The Council's stipend: 3 Coin. 0 who walked from you are still inside the walls. A letter of service lands on your desk: Apothecary's Boy. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 4 Coin in hand.

journal.title: A Watchman Hurt
journal.text: Beadle Pietersz was set upon outside the Watch-house. They will be in the Abbey hospital for a while.

journal.title: New Case: The Death of Endres Ebner
journal.text: The crier's song brings the first of them to your door before the ink is dry. Endres Ebner sickened over a month: hair coming out in the comb. Everyone called it a wasting. The coroner's book calls it something else. In the sickroom, a bottle of "tonic".

journal.title: Taken: Griet Claesz
journal.text: The sergeants take them at the city gate, one foot on the carrier's wagon. The charge is full proof. Now it is for the sworn men.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over the Molenaar Warehouse. You find: A cobble with a note tied to it, A Chewed Clove.  The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: Delivered: Sketch-book
journal.text: It arrives by carrier in a crate with the wrong name on it. It works perfectly.

journal.title: Sickness
journal.text: A cough from the river, a heat behind the eyes. The Warrens give it to everyone in the end. Deal with it in Rest before the clock runs out.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: Regina Kuiper walks the round without complaint. The Council's ledger reads your name.

journal.title: Back on the Round
journal.text: Apothecary's Boy Vos is out of the Abbey hospital and back at the Watch-house.

journal.title: Griet Claesz Cracks
journal.text: You slide The Inventory across the table. Griet Claesz's composure goes, all at once, like a dam breaking.

journal.title: Clear Your Head
journal.text: You take the string off the walls. You write to your sister. You make yourself admit that you might be wrong. It helps.

journal.title: Week 14
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 2. The Council's stipend: 3 Coin. Somebody who walked from a case of yours bought a round in the Stews and drank to your health, the wrong way. A Dominican, white habit under a black cloak, has taken rooms at the Abbey and asked for the Rolls. The Bishop sent for him. He is called the Inquisitor, and he does not answer to you. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 7 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Fever
journal.text: You stand in the Market outside the Watch-house for an hour and cannot make yourself go in. Your hands will not stop shaking. You need rest, and soon.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at the Molenaar Warehouse. You find: The Message, A Tavern Token: the washhouse in Weber Row. The first name in the casebook: Hans Seiler.

journal.title: The Bishop's Invitation: Send your regrets
journal.text: The Council is pleased. The Bishop's chaplain stops greeting you in the street. (The Council's favour)

journal.title: The Bishop's Invitation
journal.text: The Bishop would be glad to see the Examiner at the cathedral on Sunday, in the front pew, where the city can see him too. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: The round hears things: a word about Fire at the Molenaar Warehouse.

journal.title: Back on the Round
journal.text: Beadle Pietersz is out of the Abbey hospital and back at the Watch-house.

journal.title: Fixation
journal.text: The walls of your study are covered in string and paper. You are certain you are right. You are certain of everything now. That should frighten you more than it does.

journal.title: Means and Moment
journal.text: Who wanted it, and who could have done it. When you lay the reason beside the chance, only one face fits both. It was Griet Claesz, a journeyman turned off. It has to be.

journal.title: Week 13
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 3 Coin. A name you let go was heard in the Red Ox this week. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 5 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Wounded
journal.text: Someone was waiting on the stair of your lodging. You remember the first blow of the cudgel and not much after.

journal.title: An Alibi
journal.text: You try Hodge Welser's story: a wedding, and forty guests who remember the dancing. It will want checking.

journal.title: New Ground: The Warrens
journal.text: Your feet take you somewhere new. Tenements stacked against the wall, and cellars under the cellars. Everyone saw nothing, and everyone knows everything. The long way round, and your legs know it.

journal.title: Delivered: Vinegar and Umbrella
journal.text: It arrives by carrier in a crate with the wrong name on it. It works perfectly.

journal.title: The Purse Is Gone
journal.text: Somebody came back for it. They will remember you left it alone. The people who left it remember.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: The round hears things: a word about Burglary at Fletcher's Pawnshop.

journal.title: New Case: Fire at the Molenaar Warehouse
journal.text: Somebody set fire to the Molenaar Warehouse a day after the refusal. It started with a cobble with a note tied to it. The message came the next morning: the name of a tavern.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over Fletcher's Pawnshop. You find: A Key, Not a Crow.  The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Week 12
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 2. The Council's stipend: 3 Coin. 0 who walked from you are still inside the walls. There is a purse on your desk. Nobody saw who left it. The ledger: 1 conviction; 1 open; 5 Coin in hand.

journal.title: A Watchman Hurt
journal.text: Apothecary's Boy Vos was set upon outside the Watch-house. They will be in the Abbey hospital for a while.

journal.title: The Rope: Regina Dyer
journal.text: The staff is broken. Regina Dyer hangs on the Ravenstone before the whole city, and the ballad-sellers have the verses printed by nones. Their band drinks to them in a cellar and to you in a different tone.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over Fletcher's Pawnshop. You find: The Carrier's Chit, A Chit from the washhouse in Weber Row.  The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: Delivered: The Apothecary's Key
journal.text: It arrives by carrier in a crate with the wrong name on it. It works perfectly.

journal.title: Guilty: Regina Dyer
journal.text: The sworn men are out for the length of a Paternoster. Regina Dyer is convicted of Hue and Cry: Regina Dyer, and the sergeants take them down to the Hole to wait for the sentence. Their name comes off the wall. The Council's thanks, with a purse attached.

journal.title: Condemned: Regina Dyer
journal.text: Regina Dyer goes down to the Hole to wait. The ladder is on your desk: Pardon, Banished, The Rope. The Council will follow your word, or its custom.

journal.title: The Petitions
journal.text: A clerk brings the forms the Council will now hear from you: instruments, rooms, a key. Each Petition in Attend with its price in Coin.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Results
journal.text: Four keys. Three are accounted for. The fourth was "lost" a month ago by someone who still comes and goes. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: Sworn In
journal.text: Regina Kuiper takes the oath at the Watch-house door. A priest without a parish. Sits. Listens. People tell him things they have never told God.

journal.title: Entered
journal.text: Four hours with the quill. By the end, even the parts that were not quite by the Carolina read as if they were.

journal.title: Healed
journal.text: The barber-surgeon takes the stitches out. You can take a blow again. Probably.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over Fletcher's Pawnshop. You find: The Key Tally.  The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: Sworn In
journal.text: Hans Vos takes the oath at the Watch-house door. Talks to jars more than people. Knows the taste of every powder in the shop and which ones he should not have tasted.

journal.title: Promoted: Bailiff
journal.text: The Council gives you the white staff and the key to the Hole's outer door. The sergeants stand when you come in. Some of them mean it. You are now Bailiff. Watch a door and go in Disguise (Explore), and Deputise a watchman with a case (Attend). The Council will send you up to 4 cases at once, and pay 3 a week.

journal.title: A Hot Dinner
journal.text: Mutton, bread, small beer, and a second helping. Your hands stop shaking somewhere around the pudding.

journal.title: An Insight: An Iron Constitution
journal.text: Hunger, fever and the black nights, and you are still at the desk. The Warrens give everything to everyone in the end, and you have found out what they cannot take. Take it to Rest.

journal.title: Taken: Regina Dyer
journal.text: The sergeants take them at first light, on their doorstep. The charge is full proof. Now it is for the sworn men.

journal.title: Week 11
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 2 Coin. Somebody who walked from a case of yours bought a round in the Stews and drank to your health, the wrong way. A letter of service lands on your desk: Sergeant of the Watch. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 11 Coin in hand.

journal.title: A Watchman Hurt
journal.text: Beadle Pietersz was set upon outside the Watch-house. They will be in the Abbey hospital for a while.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Hunger
journal.text: You cannot remember your last hot meal. Your hands have started to shake on the stairs. Deal with it in Rest before the clock runs out.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: The night-watchman keeps his hours in his head. Two, quiet. Three, the shutter open. Somebody knew the house, and somebody was in and out between the bells. The back room stayed locked, and the hard way in wore you out.

journal.title: Interrupted
journal.text: Whatever you were working on is gone before you finish. The city does not wait.

journal.title: Regina Dyer Cracks
journal.text: You lay A Curved Scratch on the table and say nothing. Regina Dyer stares at it for a long time. Then they start to talk.

journal.title: A Room at the Swan: Take the room
journal.text: You sleep like the dead and wake like the living. (Weariness lifts)

journal.title: A Room at the Swan
journal.text: The landlord of the Swan, who owes the Watch a kindness, offers a room with a fire and a door that locks. One night. Tonight. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: The Pawnbroker's Book: Buy the page
journal.text: A page in a bad hand, with a name on it that you were going to have to find the hard way. (A token that names a name)

journal.title: The Pawnbroker's Book
journal.text: A pawnbroker keeps a book of everything that came through his door this week, and who brought it. Something from your case is in it. He would part with the page. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. The blade was a chisel, chipped at one corner. Find the chisel, find the burglar. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: The Council Takes Notice
journal.text: A letter on heavy paper under the city's seal: the Council will see you about the office of Bailiff. Attend on them, in a clean collar.

journal.title: Promoted: Sworn Examiner
journal.text: You swear the oath in the Council chamber with your hand on the Carolina, and the clerk writes your name under the last Examiner's, which has a line through it. You are now Sworn Examiner. A magistrate will seal a Writ for you (an Accused with cause, in Explore), and the Council sends you more. The Council will send you up to 3 cases at once, and pay 2 a week.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at Fletcher's Pawnshop. The back shutter has been forced with something flat and patient, and the strongbox stands open like a mouth. You come away with The Pried Shutter, The Inventory. A name for the casebook: Griet Claesz. The back room stayed locked, and the hard way in wore you out.

journal.title: Week 10
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. A name you let go was heard in the Red Ox this week. The ledger: 2 convictions; 2 open; 10 Coin in hand.

journal.title: An Informer Is Burned
journal.text: Moth was dragged into an alley and asked who they had been talking to. Nobody has seen them since.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: The Fire: Gregory Schmidt
journal.text: The staff is broken, and the fire follows, before the whole city. It takes most of the morning. The crowd is very quiet by the end, and so is the Market for a week after. The underworld learns your name from it.

journal.title: Hands and Hours
journal.text: What was left behind, and who could have been there to leave it. The marks narrow the door until only one person fits through it. It was Regina Dyer, the fugitive. It has to be.

journal.title: A Word
journal.text: Moth counts the coin twice before talking. It is worth it. They know something about Burglary at Fletcher's Pawnshop.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: You covered the desk yourself while they walked.

journal.title: New Case: Burglary at Fletcher's Pawnshop
journal.text: No broken glass at Ursel Bader's. Whoever came in overnight used the stair from the rooms above, and left with three silver spoons and a ledger. A neighbour reports seeing the candle go on and off again, as if someone knew the house. You were warned, and you were ready: the scene is fresh, and you already have a name.

journal.title: Guilty: Gregory Schmidt
journal.text: The sworn men are out for the length of a Paternoster. Gregory Schmidt is convicted of False Coin in Gerber's Tavern, and the sergeants take them down to the Hole to wait for the sentence. The Council's thanks, with a purse attached.

journal.title: Condemned: Gregory Schmidt
journal.text: Gregory Schmidt goes down to the Hole to wait. The ladder is on your desk: Pardon, A Fine, Branded, The Fire. The Council will follow your word, or its custom. Pleas arrive with the morning: The Guild's Plea, A Family's Plea.

journal.title: The Market
journal.text: The stallholders know your face now. The Quarter is yours to walk: put it in Explore with Health for a round, or with a case to look for its people there.

journal.title: The Rival Exposed
journal.text: Two hours of polite questions, and a name they did not want spoken: a moneylender, a widow, a file of their own. The Council reads the file in silence and sends the Harbourmaster's Examiner back to the Customs House. Your name is spoken in the chamber, warmly for once.

journal.title: Nothing Tonight
journal.text: Moth takes the coin and has nothing for it. "Next week," they say.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without the Vinegar and Umbrella, you only get part of it. The same hand as the one in the Rolls from the first case. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: The Rope: Dorcas Webster
journal.text: The staff is broken. Dorcas Webster hangs on the Ravenstone before the whole city, and the ballad-sellers have the verses printed by nones. The crowd goes home satisfied.

journal.title: Nothing Tonight
journal.text: Moth takes the coin and has nothing for it. "Next week," they say.

journal.title: The Council Takes Notice
journal.text: A letter on heavy paper under the city's seal: the Council will see you about the office of Sworn Examiner. Attend on them, in a clean collar.

journal.title: Guilty: Dorcas Webster
journal.text: The sworn men are out for the length of a Paternoster. Dorcas Webster is convicted of Burglary at the Molenaar House, and the sergeants take them down to the Hole to wait for the sentence. The Council's thanks, with a purse attached. At the court door Bartel Mercer presses a coin into your hand and will not take it back. An honest fee.

journal.title: Condemned: Dorcas Webster
journal.text: Dorcas Webster goes down to the Hole to wait. The ladder is on your desk: Pardon, A Fine, Pillory, Banished, Branded, The Rope. The Council will follow your word, or its custom. Pleas arrive with the morning: A Family's Plea.

journal.title: An Insight: The Old Examiner's Method
journal.text: Full proof before the Blood Court, and the judge asked who taught you. Nobody did. But in the drawer of your desk is a leaf in the last examiner's hand, and reading it now, you understand it. Take it to Rest.

journal.title: Week 9
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. 1 who walked from you are still inside the walls. The ledger: no case closed; 1 open; 6 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Wounded
journal.text: Someone was waiting on the stair of your lodging. You remember the first blow of the cudgel and not much after.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over a Rented Garret in The Abbey Close. You find: The Abandoned Garret.  The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: Taken: Gregory Schmidt
journal.text: The sergeants take them at the Red Ox, mid-sentence. The charge is full proof. Now it is for the sworn men.

journal.title: An Evening Off
journal.text: You walk to the mill-race and back without once thinking about a case. On the way home you think about one. It is a start.

journal.title: Let It Go
journal.text: You take the papers off the wall. You go to the players in the inn-yard. You do not think about the case for three whole hours.

journal.title: A Weakness Found
journal.text: Two hours of polite questions, and a name they did not want spoken: a moneylender, a widow, a file of their own. They will be careful for a week. One more, and you will have them.

journal.title: Stress
journal.text: You wake at the same hour every night with the same case behind your eyes. You have started to snap at the sergeant. Deal with it in Rest before the clock runs out.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over a Rented Garret in The Abbey Close. You find: A Curved Scratch.  The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: Endres Pietersz walks the round without complaint. The Council's ledger reads your name.

journal.title: The Trail Fades
journal.text: Smoke After Curfew has faded beyond use.

journal.title: Taken: Dorcas Webster
journal.text: The sergeants take them at first light, on their doorstep. The charge is full proof. Now it is for the sworn men.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Week 8
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. Somebody who walked from a case of yours bought a round in the Stews and drank to your health, the wrong way. The Harbourmaster has sent an examiner of his own. The ledger: no case closed; 3 open; 7 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Which Stair Is Yours
journal.text: A man has been asking in the Red Ox which stair is yours. He was not asking for the landlord.

journal.title: The Harbourmaster's Examiner
journal.text: Piet Wieland has the Harbourmaster's letter and a desk in the Customs House. The Harbourmaster wants the Council to see it has a choice. They will work your cases from the other side: close them first, spoil your scenes, pay your witnesses to forget. Question them, buy them, frighten them, or shadow them; find their weakness twice and the Council sends them home.

journal.title: The Trail Fades
journal.text: Partial: The Hand Read has faded beyond use.

journal.title: The Purse Is Gone
journal.text: Somebody came back for it. They will remember you left it alone. The people who left it remember.

journal.title: Means and Moment
journal.text: Who wanted it, and who could have done it. When you lay the reason beside the chance, only one face fits both. It was Dorcas Webster, the night porter. It has to be.

journal.title: An Insight: The Sergeant's Patience
journal.text: The sergeant has seen every examiner burn out the same way. He shows you how he sits down between things: how he lets a case go for the length of a pipe, and comes back to it. Take it to Rest.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at a Rented Garret in The Abbey Close. You find: Disturbed Dust, The Old Case. The first name in the casebook: Regina Dyer. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: The Trail Fades
journal.text: The Hours has faded beyond use.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: Endres Pietersz walks the round without complaint. The Council's ledger reads your name.

journal.title: The Trail Fades
journal.text: Partial: The Blade Read has faded beyond use.

journal.title: The Beggar at the Door: Give her a Coin
journal.text: The child gets bread. She tells you who came and went, and the clerks get a story about you. (The Crowd and Dread ease; her word on the case)

journal.title: The Beggar at the Door
journal.text: A woman with a child on her hip has been at the Watch-house door since prime. She does not ask for anything. She just stands there, where the Council's clerks can see her, and she has seen everyone who passed. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: A Reason
journal.text: You let Dorcas Webster talk about Bartel Mercer. Their voice changes when they do. The porter was turned off last month and never paid his last wages.

journal.title: The Trail Fades
journal.text: The Inventory has faded beyond use.

journal.title: A Sighting
journal.text: Moth leans in. "Regina Dyer. I know where they sleep."

journal.title: Sighting: Regina Dyer
journal.text: Moth has seen Regina Dyer. Regina Dyer has been seen again. They walked once. The trail is warm, for now.

journal.title: Let It Go
journal.text: You take the papers off the wall. You go to the players in the inn-yard. You do not think about the case for three whole hours.

journal.title: Week 7
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. A name you let go was heard in the Red Ox this week. There is a purse on your desk. Nobody saw who left it. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 7 Coin in hand.

journal.title: A Word
journal.text: Moth counts the coin twice before talking. It is worth it. They know something about Burglary at the Molenaar House.

journal.title: A Word
journal.text: Moth counts the coin twice before talking. It is worth it. They know something about Burglary at the Molenaar House.

journal.title: The Cough Clears
journal.text: Bitter bark in wine, two days sweating under every blanket you own, and on the third morning the river smells like a river again.

journal.title: A Word
journal.text: Moth counts the coin twice before talking. It is worth it. They know something about Burglary at the Molenaar House.

journal.title: Cleared: Barbel Tucher
journal.text: You try Barbel Tucher's story. It holds: a bed in the Abbey hospital. Strike one name from the casebook.

journal.title: Let It Go
journal.text: You take the papers off the wall. You go to the players in the inn-yard. You do not think about the case for three whole hours.

journal.title: A Word
journal.text: Moth counts the coin twice before talking. It is worth it. They know something about Burglary at the Molenaar House.

journal.title: Marked: Moth
journal.text: Somebody in the Warrens has asked, by name, who Moth's friend at the Watch-house is. They stop coming to the bench. Guard them in Attend with a watchman, or the next time they are asked it will not be politely.

journal.title: Week 6
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 12 Coin in hand.

journal.title: The Coquille
journal.text: You have seen the same advocate at every hearing, the same faces at every cellar door. Behind the city's crime there is a court, a barrel for a throne, and a king. They call it the Coquille. Go in Disguise to get at its books. The name is Regina Dyer. It is not in your Rolls. It will be.

journal.title: A Word
journal.text: Moth counts the coin twice before talking. It is worth it. They know something about Burglary at the Molenaar House.

journal.title: Sickness
journal.text: A cough from the river, a heat behind the eyes. The Warrens give it to everyone in the end. Deal with it in Rest before the clock runs out.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. Cheap leaf, sold at two shops in the city. Both keep a slate for regulars.

journal.title: Breakthrough
journal.text: What the witnesses said, and why anyone would want this. Suddenly the story tells itself. It was Gregory Schmidt, a tavern-keeper. It has to be.

journal.title: A Word
journal.text: Moth counts the coin twice before talking. It is worth it. They know something about Burglary at the Molenaar House.

journal.title: An Insight: A Word in the Right Ear
journal.text: An informer trusts you now, which in this city is rarer than gold. They tell you which tapster to buy, and which to be seen buying. Take it to Rest.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over the Molenaar House. You find: Pipe Ash in the Study, A Shell on the Sill, The Second Key. A neighbour, leaning on the gate, offers a name: Dorcas Webster. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: A Purse on the Desk: Pocket it
journal.text: Silver is silver. Somebody now believes you can be bought, because you can. (+3 Coin; the Council's eye)

journal.title: A Purse on the Desk
journal.text: Nobody saw who left it. Three Coin, good silver, and a note with the name of a case on it and nothing else. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: The Confessor: Ask him to point
journal.text: He does not say a word. He looks, once, at a door, and goes back inside to pray for both of you. (A token that names a name; the Bishop frowns)

journal.title: The Confessor
journal.text: A priest of the parish asks for a word. Someone told him something under the seal, and it is eating him. He will not break the seal. He might point. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Pocketed
journal.text: Three weeks' stipend in worn silver. It sits in your coat like a stone. Somewhere, somebody writes your name in a ledger.

journal.title: Cleared: Afra Chandler
journal.text: Afra Chandler has an answer, and it is a good one: a game of tables with a sergeant of the Watch. They are cleared.

journal.title: Week 5
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. There is a purse on your desk. Nobody saw who left it. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 9 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over Gerber's Tavern. You find: A Lombard's Chit.  The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: The round hears things: a word about False Coin in Gerber's Tavern.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without the Vinegar and Umbrella, you only get part of it. Vinegar brings up the hand that pressed it: a thumb, and a missing nail. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over Gerber's Tavern. You find: A broken mould. A neighbour, leaning on the gate, offers a name: Walburg Bicker. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: A Deposition
journal.text: You sit. You listen. You let the silence do the work. Eventually the Tiler says: "A shell on the hat, like the pilgrims."

journal.title: Trouble at the Swan: Break it up
journal.text: Two carters in the cells and a tapster who remembers who kept his window. He pays in silver. (+2 Coin from a grateful tapster)

journal.title: Trouble at the Swan
journal.text: The round passes the Swan as two carters go through its window. The tapster is shouting your name. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Week 4
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 6 Coin in hand.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: You covered the desk yourself while they walked.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Hands and Hours
journal.text: What was left behind, and who could have been there to leave it. The marks narrow the door until only one person fits through it. You know what kind of person. Not yet which.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at Gerber's Tavern. You find: Smoke After Curfew, A Plaster Mould. The first name in the casebook: Sibylla de Groot. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: Endres Pietersz walks the round without complaint. The Council's ledger reads your name.

journal.title: A Reason
journal.text: You let Gregory Schmidt talk about Claes Fletcher. Their voice changes when they do. The tavern passes more coin in a night than the Mint in a week, and nobody looks at it by candlelight.

journal.title: Week 3
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 4 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without the Vinegar and Umbrella, you only get part of it. Under vinegar and the red umbrella the hand comes up whole: a thumb with a scar across it. Good enough for the Court. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: A Warning
journal.text: "Burglary," says Moth, "in The Market. Soon. Don't ask me how I know."

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over the Molenaar House. You find: Marks on the Sill. A neighbour, leaning on the gate, offers a name: Barbel Tucher. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: New Case: False Coin in Gerber's Tavern
journal.text: Somebody in the city has a furnace going on Sunday, when the forges are cold: smoke from a chimney where nobody lives. The Mintmaster is certain of the die. In a midden nearby, a broken mould. You were warned, and you were ready: the scene is fresh, and you already have a name.

journal.title: The Clerk's Favour: Keep the file
journal.text: The clerk's smile does not reach his eyes. Your name is spoken in the chamber, not warmly, and in the lanes, warmly. (Standing rises)

journal.title: The Clerk's Favour
journal.text: The Council's clerk lingers after delivering the stipend. A councillor's son was found where he should not have been, with people he should not have known. There is a file. It would be a kindness if there were not. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: The Day-book
journal.text: A woman reports her husband missing. He is at the Red Ox. You find him in ten minutes.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Sworn In
journal.text: Endres Pietersz takes the oath at the Watch-house door. A parish beadle with a staff and a loud voice. Knocks on doors without complaining and whips beggars without being asked.

journal.title: Week 2
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The ledger: no case closed; 1 open; 4 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: The night-watchman keeps his hours in his head. Two, quiet. Three, the shutter open. Somebody knew the house, and somebody was in and out between the bells. The back room stayed locked, and the hard way in wore you out.

journal.title: The Round
journal.text: A stallholder shakes your hand. A boy spits at your boots. An ordinary round.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. The blade was a chisel, chipped at one corner. Find the chisel, find the burglar. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: A Warning
journal.text: "Coining," says Moth, "in The Market. Soon. Don't ask me how I know."

journal.title: The Tiler's Word: A Coin for his trouble
journal.text: He saw a face, and he will say so again where it counts. (A Witness who saw it)

journal.title: The Tiler's Word
journal.text: A tiler was on his ladder across the lane when it happened, mending a roof that did not need mending. He says so to anyone with a coin, and now he is saying it to you. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at the Molenaar House. The back shutter has been forced with something flat and patient, and the strongbox stands open like a mouth. You come away with The Pried Shutter, The Inventory. A name for the casebook: Afra Chandler. The back room stayed locked, and the hard way in wore you out.

journal.title: After the Burial
journal.text: You took the Council's letter the week after the burial. The man who did it walks the Hill in a good coat. Start with what is on the desk; it all leads to the same door in the end.

journal.title: New Case: Burglary at the Molenaar House
journal.text: Bartel Mercer is not sure when it happened: during the wedding downstairs. Only the cellar hatch was touched, and only the deeds and the coin taken. A neighbour reports seeing a tradesman's cart that no tradesman came from. Somebody knew the house.

choice.title: The Pawnbroker's Book
choice.text: A pawnbroker keeps a book of everything that came through his door this week, and who brought it. Something from your case is in it. He would part with the page.

options.label: Buy the page
options.text: A page in a bad hand, with a name on it that you were going to have to find the hard way.
options.gain: A token that names a name

options.label: Threaten his licence
options.text: He gives you the page and a look. The Council's clerk hears how the Examiner does business.
options.gain: The token; the Council hears of it

options.label: Leave it
options.text: You do not deal with pawnbrokers. The word gets round that you do not.
